sampling.pipeModel: solid cylinder at the member's own stock_build radius: 5.0 mm x180, 7.0 mm x36

octet.derivation: crush: 3*p*SF*V/(96*L), the octet's own hydrostatic share. The standalone article only puts 1125 N through it (Q/3 at a square centre through 4 struts at 45 deg); this is the array's load, which is what the demonstrator exists to prove.

rim.derivation: film, in-plane: hoop for the two hexagon rings a hexagon-hexagon edge belongs to. A square-hexagon edge takes 3549 N. No crush share: the rim vertices are dual sites and no rim member is an octet strut.

spoke.derivation: film, in-plane: the hexagon's radial tributary, sqrt(3)/2 * q * a with q = T*cos(alpha) = 6874 N/m. Bending governs it, not this (film_edge_loads rows 3 and 4).

tripodProp.derivation: film, normal: the hub's H/3 through 3 <100> props at 54.74 deg = p*a^2/2. Exact — nothing else at a hub can take it.

vertexTieInPlane.derivation: film: the square's share of a rim vertex, p*a^2/3, plus the square panel's in-plane radial tributary q*a/sqrt(2). The largest short-member demand in the article.

vertexTieInward.derivation: film, normal: a rim vertex's 2*H/9 + Q/6 resolves onto its <100> prop as p*a^2/2, the same value as the hub's tripod reached independently.

0.member: rim edge, hexagons UNBRACED (the design as it stood)

buildOrder.clearanceRuleMm: r_i + r_j from stock_build per member

capacityGaps.standIn: the TDS TENSILE allowable interpolated on elevation, conservative for a confined land and the same substitution spigotDirect makes
capacityGaps.experiment: BEARING: print one socket in its own article frame, press a cut tube stub into it through a load cell and record load against embedment past 3376 N. The load at 0.10 mm embedment IS the bearing allowable this margin is substituting sigma_allow for, measured on the confined land rather than on a dogbone

capacityGaps.standIn: mu = 1.0 on the measured rib crest contact at the material's own allowable — a ceiling, so it can fail a row and never pass one
capacityGaps.experiment: FRICTION: print two ribbed spigots, slide the specified tube on to full engagement and pull it straight back off on the same load cell, dry and unbonded, at the as-assembled interference. Peak load / (rib contact area x sigma_allow) is mu for this pair; anything at or under mu = 1.0 leaves the bound above standing

capacityGaps.standIn: the whole root section at a uniform 92 MPa, the strongest strength the TDS reports in any direction — a ceiling, same rule
capacityGaps.experiment: SHEAR: short-beam shear (ASTM D2344) on coupons printed in BOTH orientations the nodes use, in-plane and across layers, so the shear allowable can be interpolated on elevation the way sigma already is. One number per orientation replaces the tensile ceiling this margin is bounded with, and it is the only one of the three that needs a fixture rather than a press

capacityGaps.standIn: gen_nodes' own 10 MPa glue line, a line and not a datasheet, applied as if it were a capacity
capacityGaps.experiment: ADHESIVE: lap-shear (ASTM D1002-style) on the actual adhesive against a printed coupon and against the tube's own surface, because the joint is bonded on both and the weaker face governs. This one is not gated as a gap — the 10 MPa line is at least a number — but it is the least defended capacity in the table

frozenParameters.note: still absent from this repository, every one of them: no measured bearing allowable, no friction coefficient, no interlaminar shear allowable, no creep knockdown; tauAllowMPa is gen_nodes' own 10 MPa glue line rather than a datasheet. What changed is that the margins no longer stop at saying so. axialBearing substitutes the TDS TENSILE allowable for the bearing allowable — the substitution spigotDirect already made — and pullOutDry and transverseShear carry UPPER BOUNDS that can fail a row and may never pass one, with the value a test would have to return printed under P16 and the test itself named on each row. Every capacity here is still short-term, dry and annealed: the TDS conditions its numbers that way, research/notes/print-reliability.md says the wet state is unmeasured by anyone for PAHT-CF, and mass-budget.py already carries BARRIER_SF = 4.0 for the film's permanent-creep case, so the convention exists and has still never been applied to the joints. A parameter stays frozen while any margin that depends on it is UNSOURCED or UNPROVEN.

advisories.name: rigidity-and-indeterminacy
lines: rigidity rank 147 = 3V-6 = 147 exactly, so static indeterminacy is 69. That is the count of members closing into ALREADY RIGID node pairs; it is order-independent and real, and it is the wrong number for assembly. 166 is the assembly number, and quoting 69 understates the problem 2.4x.

advisories.name: elastic-slack-budget
lines: gap-opening flexibility 8.8146e-05 to 1.7239e-04 mm/N, so opening a gap by the full 20 mm stub costs 116,019 to 226,896 N. 200 N of hand force opens 0.0176 to 0.0345 mm; 0 of 216 members exceed 0.1 mm on the finished article. That is why the closing ends carry a 2 mm pilot and not a shortened stub plus optimism: 'just spring it in' is the natural response to P1 and it is wrong by four orders of magnitude. Even the pilot's own 2 mm would cost 11,602 N to spring, which is why it is swung in instead. This is a pin-jointed LOWER bound on stiffness.

length error is not free: 5,801 to 11,345 N per mm of it. 0.10 mm of cut error locks in 580 to 1,134 N, and 0.197 to 0.386 mm locks in the whole 2238 N demand of the spoke — the smallest of the six family demands, and therefore the member with the least room for a locked-in force. Holding the locked-in force under 10% of demand needs every cut, and every printed base, inside 0.020 to 0.039 mm — finer than one FDM layer, and finer than the margins two of the passing proofs pass on. It is published as a tolerance column on cutList and gated by nothing, because no shop capability is cited anywhere in this repository to hold it to.

and every number above is isothermal, dry and short-term: MATERIALS.PAHT_XY carries ['E', 'name', 'orthotropic', 'printable', 'rho', 'sigma', 'source'] and none of ['cte', 'moistureGrowth', 'creepKnockdown', 'durationOfLoad']. At 5,801 to 11,345 N per mm of length error, a strain that changes a 38.0 mm printed load path by one FDM layer is worth hundreds of newtons of self-stress in a frame with 166 redundant loops. No coefficient is invented here to price it: the vacuum load is permanent and every capacity in this file is a short-term ISO 527 tensile number, which is stated on every margin.

the bow alternative: 20 mm of end shortening on a 251 mm member needs 45.08 mm of bow and 3.54% surface strain; 20 mm of end shortening on a 177 mm member needs 37.90 mm of bow and 5.95% surface strain; 3 mm of end shortening on a 177 mm member needs 14.68 mm of bow and 2.31% surface strain, against roughly 1.5% ultimate. Even 3 mm breaks a tie.

advisories.name: build-order-insertion-access
lines: against the FINISHED article 105 of 216 members have no straight-line escape. Inside-out — members sorted by ascending |midpoint|, ties broken by (family, u, v) for determinism — blocks 0 at their own turn. Outside-in blocks 12. The order is therefore part of the contract and is emitted as buildOrder; it is not left to the builder. Clearance is per pair, r_i + r_j over the SKUs stock_build specifies (5.0 mm x180, 7.0 mm x36), and node bodies are covered by P9's envelope bound rather than modelled here.

data.clearanceRuleMm: r_i + r_j from stock_build per member

advisories.name: free-end-sweep
lines: along the 50-member spanning tree, walked in discovery order, the tightest free-end retraction leaves 101.397 mm of clearance (member (-1, 2, 0)-(-1, 1, 0) at 0 mm of retraction) against a required 11.10 mm centre-line separation. This is the only legal motion in the build: the tree assembles freely and the whole problem is the 166 members that close it. The margin is recorded so a later change to stub, base or the graph is caught the moment it stops passing. Each placed member is at its own specified radius, not at one global pipe_od.

advisories.name: pricing-the-recommended-fix
lines: 332 closing member-ends are engaged 2 mm instead of 20, which removes 153 g of printed spigot (measured section 24.16 mm2, uniform to 0.000 mm2 between the two stations) and is what makes the article assemblable at all. It costs pull-out: mean bonded area falls from 511.5 mm2 at a tree end to 76.3 at a closing one, so at the same 10 MPa line a closing end holds 763 N against 5115. The cup is what keeps that from being 503 N — the spigot alone — and it costs nothing to carry, where the external sleeves that would restore the same capture weigh 113 g over 166 members.

Above the seat band the tightest the field comes to a pipe surface anywhere in the article is 0.1500 mm (at n19.a00), which is exactly the 0.15 mm design gap — attained at BOTH walls of the band at once, the pipe's bore against the spigot crest at id/2 and the pipe's outside against the slot wall at od/2, since each is drawn one clearance clear of the tube. It equals `clearance` by construction and will read so at every end for as long as nothing intrudes: this is the sign test the paragraph above promises, not an independent measurement of the fit. Foreign nodes are excluded here and covered by P9's envelope bound.

proofs.name: land-integrity
proofs.headline: 108 members lie in a shared face (decided: not a mating surface); 0 bore/land pairs breach
details: 108 of 216 members (rim 36, spoke 48, tie 24) lie exactly in a face plane shared by both their nodes — each a pipe centred ON the plane, standing 5.00 mm proud on both sides (7.00 mm on the 36 rim members). That is NOT a defect and is no longer a fail key: the 86 lands on 38 nodes are a print datum and a film bond plane, not a bearing face between cells. Two finished articles cannot be brought flush — they stop 14 mm apart on the rim pipes — and nothing in the design asks them to: kelvin_lattice_counts shows this whole boundary apparatus is the ODD-n case, and at even n the lattice runs straight through the hexagon planes with the film bonded to its crossings. The inter-cell joint is E1's open question and it is not a butt joint on these lands.

bore mouths: (arm, land) angles beta = 0.0000 deg x24, 35.2644 deg x96, 45.0000 deg x96, 54.7356 deg x120, so the steepest of them needs r_bore*tan(beta) = 2.616 mm of setback, and gen_nodes.bore_start gives that arm 4.250 mm. No bore opens onto a land.

proofs.name: printability
proofs.headline: 13 landless nodes, 42 downward arms, 0 arm ends into air
details: 13 of 51 nodes lie on no cell face, so they carry no mating land and print_frame() has no datum to inherit. It no longer returns the identity for them: it measures all six lattice bed normals on the joint's own field and takes the least island volume, then the most bed contact, then the most sum cos^2(elevation). Each one's chosen normal is in the manifest as bedNormalArticle. This key counts nodes with no MATING land and cannot reach zero — an interior node has no cell face to seat on — so it is a census of the joints that had to be oriented rather than seated, not a verdict on the print.

42 of 432 arms have their tip below their root (7 at -90 deg, 35 at -45 deg), all on those same nodes — AND THAT IS NOT THE PRINTABILITY MEASURE. An arm aimed down whose tip reaches the plate is a tower and prints support-free; four of equal length are a four-legged stand. What cannot print is an end that starts with nothing under it, and minimising THIS count actively produces those: the frames with the fewest downward arms are the ones that put a single long tree arm straight down, which drops the bed 36 mm below the node and leaves every other downward feature hanging in the gap. The count stays gated so that no frame change goes undeclared; it is not the verdict. Over the 13 joints that had a frame to choose, measured on the search grid every candidate was built on: the frames taken cost 42 downward arms and 2864 mm3 of island, the frames with the fewest downward arms would cost 28 and 7114 — a third fewer arms pointing down for 2.5x the material with nothing under it. manifest.overhangAreaFrac is not the verdict either, and this is the cleanest demonstration of it: the joint carrying the most material with nothing under it (node_01_lattice.stl, 716 mm3) scores 0.143 on it, while a joint with 0.0 mm3 of island scores 0.128. An area fraction over the whole mesh cannot see an island, because an island is small and the mesh is large.

every wall the part has clears perimeters x nozzle = 1.20 mm (thinnest measured 1.44 mm = 2.40 extrusion widths at 0.6 mm). lipWallMm is not the 1.6 mm parameter: the slot's outer radius is 5.15 and the lip's is 6.60, so the wall the parameters describe is 1.45 mm = 2.42 extrusion widths, a fraction no slicer lays — and over the seated pipe it measures 1.89 mm, because the lip stops short (P7).

what actually decides the print, measured on the extraction grid by gen_nodes.bed_support() and gated per node in the contract: 0 of 432 arm ends start with nothing beneath them, 5678 mm3 of material cannot be built up from the bed at 45 degrees per layer, least bed contact 6.2 mm2. None of the three is a fraction, because the fraction is what hid this.

proofs.name: demand-provenance
proofs.headline: 0 ends with no derived axial demand, equilibrium residual 8079.5 N
details: every one of the 432 member-ends carries an axial demand derived from the load path that puts it there, at SF 1.5: octet 3376 N, rim 4477 N, spoke 2238 N, tripodProp 4775 N, vertexTieInPlane 5038 N, vertexTieInward 4775 N. The 432 ends used to be priced at one number — the octet's — which was right for 120 of them, 72 rim ends too high a class of load (the rim vertices are dual-lattice sites, so no rim member is an octet strut and it can carry no crush at all) and simply absent on the 96 spoke ends.

stock_build sizes all 72 short members at tieDemandN 5031 N, the governing one; the 144 tie ends prove at their own — 5038 N in plane, 4775 N inward and at the tripod. The purchase is therefore 5.4% conservative on the members that are not the governing one, which is what buying one SKU costs.

node equilibrium residual, member demands against the film shares they were derived from: max 8079.5 N over 51 nodes (hexHub 0.0, lattice 6366.8, rimVertex 8079.5). Each face pushes inward along its own normal at SF — hexagon 8271 N to its hub and 2757 N to each of six vertices, square 3183 N to its centre and 1592 N to each of four — and the members react it.

IT DOES NOT CLOSE, AND THE PARTS THAT SHOULD, DO. 9 of 51 nodes balance to under 0.05 N: every hexagon hub (the H/3 through three props at 54.74 deg is the one exact reaction in the article) and the centre lattice node, whose 12 octet arms are opposed pairs. 12 more sit at 3376.5 N, which is ONE octet strut's demand to the newton — those are the lattice nodes whose outward partner leaves the article, and in an array it continues into the next cell. The rest is the two modelling choices: the octet carries the ARRAY's crush (3376 N against the 1125 N a standalone cell actually puts through it), and at a rim vertex the film's in-plane pull is carried in full by the rim as hoop AND in full by the radial member, because that split is genuinely indeterminate and sizing both is the honest envelope. Count that pull once and the 24 rim vertices balance exactly; this proof does not do that, because the envelope is what the members are built to.

proofs.name: margins-are-gated
proofs.headline: axialBearing 432, bondShear 356, localBuckling 24, marginsUnproven 244, pressFit 432, pullOutDry 332, spigotBending 216, spigotDirect 432, transverseShear 72
details: 2296 of 3888 margins fail: axialBearing 432/432 (worst x0.1337 at n19.a00), bondShear 356/432 (worst x0.0768 at n19.a00), localBuckling 24/432 (worst x0.9107 at n19.a00), pressFit 432/432 (worst x0.9000 at n00.a00), pullOutDry 332/432 (worst x0.1024 at n19.a00), spigotBending 216/432 (worst x0.0028 at n19.a00), spigotDirect 432/432 (worst x0.1694 at n19.a00), transverseShear 72/432 (worst x0.5752 at n19.a00)

verdict census by margin: axialBearing FAIL:432; bondShear FAIL:356 PASS:76; localBuckling FAIL:24 PASS:408; pressFit FAIL:432; printability PASS:432; pullOutDry FAIL:332 UNPROVEN:100; spigotBending FAIL:216 NO DEMAND:216; spigotDirect FAIL:432; transverseShear FAIL:72 NO DEMAND:216 UNPROVEN:144

UNSOURCED is not PASS and neither is UNPROVEN: 0 margins carry a demand with no capacity at all and 244 carry only a bound that did not decide them, and both counts now gate as marginsUnsourced and marginsUnproven. Every one of those rows names the experiment that would settle it in margins.<path>.experimentThatWouldSettleIt; the parameters those capacities depend on stay frozen until it is run — see frozenParameters in the report.

the two bounded paths, in the units their test would report. DRY CAPTURE would need mu 0.26-9.76 over 432 ends, and 332 of them need mu above 1.0, which is not a number any bench test returns for a thermoplastic on a wound carbon tube — those are settled against the joint and no measurement reopens them. TRANSVERSE SHEAR would need a uniform allowable of 37-160 MPa on a material whose strongest measured strength in ANY direction is 92 MPa and whose interlayer tensile is 47.

three capacities that used to be UNSOURCED are derived now, and the two that are only BOUNDED say so on every row: axialBearing substitutes the TDS tensile allowable for the bearing allowable nobody has measured, the same substitution spigotDirect makes; pullOutDry is bounded above at mu = 1.0 on the measured rib crest contact; transverseShear is bounded above at the root section carrying a uniform 92 MPa. A bound may only fail a row, never pass one — see margin()'s docstring for why that asymmetry is the whole point of having them.
